chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Farra', from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not know that Jibra'il was from Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, except through divine direction (tawfiq).

key_terms.التَّوْفِيقِ: Divine direction, success, or enabling grace from God.
key_terms.جِبْرِئِيلُ: The archangel Gabriel, the messenger of revelation.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Exalted, an honorific title for God.

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad know that Jibra'il was from Allah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to clarify the nature of prophetic revelation, distinguishing between innate knowledge and knowledge granted through divine facilitation (tawfiq). This underscores the Shia theological principle that while the Prophet is infallible, his reception of the angel Jibra'il and the subsequent message is entirely dependent on Allah's will and direction, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in the realm of knowledge.
